newsitem.title: USA: Josephine may be hurricane before hitting Florida.
newsitem.headline: Josephine may be hurricane before hitting Florida.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine neared hurricane strength as it dashed across the Gulf of Mexico on Monday towards Florida's flood-prone coast where evacuations began, the National Hurricane Centre said.
"It is expected to make hurricane before landfall and to go ashore somewhere in the warning areas tonight (Monday)," said National Hurricane Centre meteorologist Trisha Wallace.

Residents of Florida's low-lying, rural coastal counties, vulnerable to the storm's expected strong tidal surge, were told to evacuate as Josephine neared hurricane strength, state emergency managers said.

"Local evacuations are in effect for the nine counties in the hurricane warning area," said Molly Payne, spokeswoman for the state Emergency Operations Centre. "The evacuations include the most vulnerable populations, including mobile home residents and people with special needs."
In towns and barrier islands along a 200 mile (320 km) stretch of the Florida Gulf Coast, residents began preparations as Josephine's threatening winds, rain and flood tides closed in.
Maximum winds rose to 70 mph (112 kph) on Monday morning, a large rise from its 50 mph (80 kph) earlier.

A hurricane warning -- alerting residents to imminent storm conditions -- was in effect for the Florida Gulf coast from the Anclote Keys to Apalachicola. A tropical storm warning was in effect south of the Anclote Keys to Venice and west of Apalachicola to Fort Walton Beach, Florida.
Forecasters also issued a tropical storm warning for the U.S. east coast from Cape Canaveral, Florida northward to Little River Inlet, South Carolina.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the centre of Josephine was located at latitude 27.6 north, longitude 86.6 west, about 175 miles (280 km) south-southwest of Apalachicola, and was moving toward the northeast at 23 mph (37 kph), forecasters said.
On its current track and speed, the centre of the storm will move onshore sometime Monday night, forecasters said.
